analysis.title: Equity Market Commentary: Slimmon's Take, November 2026
key_insights: Andrew Slimmon argues the consensus October playbook (seasonal weakness, midterm-year weakness, rotation from growth and cyclicals into defensives for October only) worked. Consumer staples and health care outperformed while technology and communications sold off hard.
He expects the playbook to shift leadership in November. After midterms, the party not in power gains seats and gridlock in DC has historically helped stocks.
Post-midterms, the S&P 500 has produced a positive 12-month return every time since 1950, with an average one-year return of +16%.

He expects a year-end rally led by the growth stocks hit in October and by some value names such as financials. He expects the October defensive winners (staples such as toothpaste and diaper makers) to go back to lagging. The team is not adding to its defensive holdings.

He sees the 'blue wave' risk to the data center buildout as campaign rhetoric. Once the election is over, strained state and local budgets and hyperscaler commitments to infrastructure, public services and education funds should make the issue fade, as in Richland Parish, Louisiana and Dona Ana County, New Mexico.
He sees no proof that AI demand is slowing and says demand for compute is accelerating.

Calendar 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth expectations rose from +14.8% at the start of the year to +32.4% as of October 30. Earnings revisions keep moving higher because the economy has been stronger than Wall Street expected.

The S&P 500 forward P/E fell from 22.1x at the start of 2026 to 18.3x. He attributes this to higher interest rates and the Fed pivoting to a rate hiking cycle. The index has not risen with earnings because the multiple has compressed.

The key question he poses is the duration and depth of the Fed tightening cycle. A long campaign of hikes would keep pushing the forward P/E lower. Only a couple of hikes over the next year would mean the multiple has probably stopped falling and earnings can lift the market.

Monthly inflation prints are the key signal. Persistently high inflation keeps the multiple falling. Prints moving toward the Fed's 2% target would stabilize the multiple and possibly re-expand it toward earlier-2026 levels. He calls this the real story for 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Expected to lead a post-midterm year-end rally after being hit hard in October. AI compute demand is described as accelerating.
Named as a value area likely to participate in a year-end rally.
October's defensive winners are expected to lag if the market pivots more optimistically. The team is not adding to defensives.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 calendar 2026 earnings growth expectation was +14.8% (consensus estimate for 2025 to 2026) at the start of the year and +32.4% as of October 30, 2026 (consensus estimate, still a forecast).
The author says the economy has been stronger than expected and has produced consistent positive earnings revisions throughout 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 22.1x at the start of 2026 despite much higher earnings expectations. The multiple is where the 2026 market pressure shows up.

macro_indicators.reading: Fed has pivoted to a rate hiking cycle
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher rates are cited as the cause of the lower P/E. The length and depth of tightening decides whether the multiple keeps falling.
Persistently high prints keep the multiple compressing. Prints moving toward 2% would stabilize or re-expand it.

risk_factors: Fed hiking cycle proves long and deep, which would keep compressing the forward P/E.
Mid-term election outcome, including a 'blue wave' that slows data center buildout.
Tech sell-off continuing, or AI demand slowing.
vol_and_positioning: October rotation into defensives (staples, health care) and out of technology and communications was crowded and consensus. The author expects it to reverse in November.
geopolitical: US mid-term elections and the possibility of a 'blue wave' that could slow the data center buildout
Reference to 'the war' as one of October's market anxieties

tension_points.bull_case: If the Fed raises rates only a couple of times over the next year, the multiple has probably stopped falling and rising earnings (S&P 500 2026 growth expectations at +32.4%) can lift the market much higher.
tension_points.bear_case: If the Fed is starting a long campaign of rate hikes, the forward P/E (now 18.3x, from 22.1x) will keep falling and suppress returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Monthly inflation prints staying persistently high rather than moving toward the Fed's 2% target.
